annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Temple of Epiphany is slightly suboptimal. Temple of Epiphany enters tapped, so playing it now (when there's no urgent need for untapped mana beyond what Sol Ring + Path of Ancestry provide) would let it be untapped on turn 3. With Swamp, the player has access to B + Sol Ring (CC) + Path (any color) = 4 mana on turn 2, which is enough to cast Kess (1UBR) if they had the colors, but Path can produce U and Sol Ring gives colorless. Actually, with Swamp + Path of Ancestry + Sol Ring, they can cast: Fellwar Stone (2 from Sol Ring), Sinister Concierge (1U from Path+Sol Ring), Bloodsoaked Champion (B from Swamp), or Spellbinding Soprano (1R from Sol Ring + Path). On turn 3 with Temple untapped, they'd have access to U/R from Temple + B from Swamp + any color from Path + CC from Sol Ring = 6 mana with UUBR available, enabling Kess (1UBR). If they play Temple now instead, on turn 3 they could play Swamp untapped and have: Temple (U/R) + Swamp (B) + Path (any) + Sol Ring (CC) = same 6 mana with full Kess colors. Either way Kess is castable turn 3. However, playing Temple now gives the scry 1 benefit immediately, which is a small advantage. The scry from Temple of Epiphany is free value that should be taken as early as possible, especially when there's no cost to doing so (both Temple and the alternative untapped land plays allow the same turn-2 and turn-3 sequences).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp as the land for turn 2.
annotations.betterLine: Play Temple of Epiphany to get the free scry 1 now, since it enters tapped anyway and Swamp can be played untapped on turn 3. The turn-2 plays (Fellwar Stone, Sinister Concierge, Bloodsoaked Champion, Spellbinding Soprano) are all still castable with Path of Ancestry + Sol Ring.

annotations.description: Casting Spellbinding Soprano in the precombat main phase is reasonable since it needs to attack to get the cost reduction trigger, and Kess is already on board. However, casting Drawn from Dreams (4 mana: 2UU) could have been a stronger play to dig for more impactful cards. With Sol Ring, Fellwar Stone, Rakdos Signet, Swamp, Path of Ancestry, and Temple of Epiphany, Grok4F has access to approximately 8 mana (2 from Sol Ring, 1 from Fellwar Stone, 1 from Rakdos Signet + 1 mana input, plus 3 lands = roughly 7-8 mana total). They could cast Drawn from Dreams to look at 7 cards and find better options. Alternatively, they could cast Preordain from the graveyard via Kess (the once-per-turn graveyard cast) to set up draws, and still cast the Soprano. The real consideration is whether Soprano attacking into a board with no blockers threatening it is worthwhile versus using Kess's ability to flashback Preordain first. Casting Soprano before combat is correct if you want to attack with it, but using Kess to flashback Preordain first (1 mana) and then casting Soprano (2 mana) and still having mana for other plays would have been better sequencing - scry 2 and draw before committing to the Soprano.
annotations.betterLine: Use Kess to flashback Preordain from graveyard first (scry 2, draw a card for U), then decide whether to cast Spellbinding Soprano or Drawn from Dreams based on what you see. This maximizes information before committing resources.

annotations.description: Attacking with a 0/1 Plant Token deals 0 damage and accomplishes nothing meaningful. The attack is pointless since the Plant can't deal damage. If anything, it risks losing the token to a blocker (though GPT4om has no creatures). Attacking Qwen3L Timmy at 33hp would be equally pointless. The only marginal argument is that it's a free attack since GPT4om has no blockers, but 0 damage is still 0 damage. The Plant token is more valuable staying back as a potential chump blocker.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked GPT4om Rookie with a 0/1 Plant Token, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack with the 0/1 Plant Token. Keep it back as a chump blocker to protect your life total. A 0-power creature attack accomplishes nothing.

annotations.description: Playing Temple of Plenty (enters tapped) instead of an untapped land means only 2 mana available in second main phase, missing the opportunity to cast Ghostly Prison this turn. At 28 life facing Bloodsoaked Champion and Kess attacks, Ghostly Prison would be very valuable for defense. The scry 1 is nice but not worth giving up a full turn of Ghostly Prison protection.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Temple of Plenty (enters tapped), leaving only 2 mana available.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest or Exotic Orchard (enters untapped) to have 3 mana available, then cast Ghostly Prison ({2}{W}) in second main phase to protect against future attacks.

annotations.description: MiMo attacks GPT4om Rookie with a 0/1 Plant Token, which deals 0 damage and accomplishes nothing offensively. GPT4om Rookie has Hostility (6/6 haste) on the battlefield, which is the biggest threat on the board. However, attacking with a 0/1 into a player who has a 6/6 is meaningless - it won't deal any damage. The only conceivable reason would be to trigger raid-like effects, but MiMo has no such cards. Attacking Qwen3L Timmy (at 28 life with no blockers) would also deal 0 damage. The attack is essentially pointless regardless of target, but choosing to attack at all with a 0/1 token that can't deal damage is slightly questionable - though the risk is minimal since GPT4om Rookie is unlikely to block with Hostility.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked GPT4om Rookie with a 0/1 Plant Token, dealing 0 combat damage.
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack at all - a 0/1 token deals no damage and the attack accomplishes nothing. Keep the Plant Token back as a potential chump blocker against threats like Hostility or Kess.

annotations.description: With only 3 lands on board and two expensive UU spells in hand (Mystic Confluence at 3UU and Extravagant Replication at 4UU), taking Exotic Orchard would have provided crucial color fixing and ensured land drops. The player instead took more card draw (Deep Analysis) and a 4-mana vehicle, risking being unable to cast their key spells on time.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Deep Analysis and Smuggler's Buggy from Drawn from Dreams
annotations.betterLine: Select Exotic Orchard and Deep Analysis - Exotic Orchard provides excellent color fixing (opponents have diverse lands producing all colors) to cast the UU-heavy spells already in hand, while Deep Analysis provides future card advantage. Smuggler's Buggy is a lower priority than reliable mana.

annotations.description: Bloodsoaked Champion (2/1) can't block, so there is zero downside to attacking with it alongside Kess. By only attacking with Kess, Grok4F left 2 free damage on the table. Additionally, attacking with Bloodsoaked Champion enables its Raid ability, allowing it to be returned from graveyard if it dies later this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Kess, Dissident Mage, leaving Bloodsoaked Champion back despite it being unable to block.
annotations.betterLine: Choose 'All attack' to also send Bloodsoaked Champion, dealing an additional 2 damage for free since it can't block anyway.

annotations.description: Grok4F Memoir discarded both lands (Swamp and Island) to Frantic Search, despite having a relatively land-light board (only 4 lands plus Path of Ancestry and Thriving Bluff = 6 lands total). Their hand contains multiple expensive spells: Extravagant Replication (6 mana), River's Rebuke (6 mana), Smuggler's Buggy (4 mana), and Mystic Confluence (5 mana). Discarding both lands makes it harder to cast these spells in a timely manner. Deep Analysis can be flashed back for just 1U + 3 life, and Extravagant Replication at 6 mana is extremely unlikely to be castable soon without more lands. Discarding one land and one of the expensive spells (like Extravagant Replication or Smuggler's Buggy) would have been better to maintain mana development while still keeping the most impactful cards.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded both Swamp and Island to Frantic Search
annotations.betterLine: Discard one land (e.g., Swamp) and one less immediately useful expensive spell (e.g., Extravagant Replication or Smuggler's Buggy), keeping a land drop available for the next turn to work toward casting the remaining high-cost spells

annotations.description: Attacking with all creatures into Gisela, Blade of Goldnight and Kalemne's Captain (5/5 vigilance). Gisela doubles damage dealt to attacking creatures while halving damage dealt to GPT4om. Kess will almost certainly die to Gisela's first strike blocking (10 damage to Kess, only 1 gets through to Gisela), and another creature dies to Kalemne's Captain. Losing Kess is devastating as it enables graveyard spellcasting, which is core to the Grixis strategy.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all 4 creatures (Kess, Bloodsoaked Champion, Sinister Concierge, Spellbinding Soprano) into Gisela + Kalemne's Captain
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Bloodsoaked Champion (returns from graveyard) and Spellbinding Soprano (for cost reduction trigger), keeping Kess and Sinister Concierge safe. Or just attack with Bloodsoaked Champion alone to enable its raid ability while preserving key creatures.
